speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I just danced you down the halls

text: - Doesn't that strike you as odd?

text:

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - I'll try and do better next time, sir.

text: I hope you like the typing job.

text: - I can do it over if you'd like.

text:

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Pretty, obedient, and knows

text:

text:

when you were just starting out?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Being nice to everybody is sick.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - Tell me, what do you need, darling?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:

text:

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: I know. Who needs a lecture, right?

text: All I'm saying is that a body like that...

text:
I know your name.
I know your brand.

text:
Selma, I hope you won't
mind my saying this...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...but I've had my eye
on you for quite a while.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
But wait!
How about some dinner...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: You look very sexy in that uniform.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Bullets, Bernie. I got those too.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: I do very well financially, you know.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - You know that stand in there?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: That's only the tip of the iceberg.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:

than anybody else in the city.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Life in the fast lane, huh?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Ready whenever you're through
rummaging, sir.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: The arrest report on the next case.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - It was about this big, fuzzy.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Oh, sir, I threw it out for you.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Miss Tracy, that was my lucky
rabbit's foot. I had it for over 25 years.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
It was just laying there,
shedding on your papers...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I'll find that rabbit's foot
if it's the last thing I do.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
It was just a silly old thing, anyway.
I'll be fine.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Cancel my hang-gliding lesson,
okay, Charley?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
If this is gonna take a while,

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Mitchell Bowers, Your Honor.
The defendant, my client.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I'm innocent. How can you arrest a man
for breaking and entering his own home?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Your Honor, we have
a bit of a legal gray area here.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - You see, Mr. Bowers here is dead.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: In the old days, we used to bury them.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Then they never gave any trouble again.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Well, Your Honor, Mr. Bowers bought
the farm in the legal sense a year ago, June.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: When his wife had him declared dead.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Mitch? When I got that letter about you,
I had to assume...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...the government knew what
they were talking about.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Marrying that little twerp
was your second.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...my client served with the Marine Corps
in Vietnam.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
He was presumed to have been
killed in action in 1973...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...but in reality, he was captured
by an enemy patrol...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...and spent the next several years
in one of their prisons.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
While I'm busting my butt trying
to escape...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...she hires some lawyer to snuff me out
so she can marry that dipstick.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Mr. Duane Sedgewick,
the lady's present husband.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Would you all approach the bench?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Why are we wasting time?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Your Honor, I can understand
Mr. Bowers' pique.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
This has been quite a shock
for me as well as...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Go on, Mr. Dipstick...
I mean...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Your Honor,
I'd like to clear up this notion...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: ...that I'm some sort of home wrecker.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: That I seduced Nora while he was away.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
That couldn't be farther
from the truth.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Like we used to say

text: "Any port in a storm." Right, Nora?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: I am telling you, it was not physical.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Mitch, from the time you left the States,
I was completely...

text: And all those years, I loved you.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Then dump Mr. Potato Head here

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I understand that
there's a lot of heartache...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:

the charge before me. Miss Tracy?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - Still looking for the foot, sir.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Would you mind putting the garbage down

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Would the counsels approach the bench?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I'm afraid there's not much
we can do here, guys.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - This is a case for a civil court.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
But if the prosecution
would drop the charges...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
It's fine. It's fine.
It's great.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
The saliva has removed
most of the jelly.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
What are the locks for? You never
needed them when I was around.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - Never had any use for them.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Never had use for poachers, either.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - lf you have, I've seen no evidence of it.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
You got 24 hours to get you and
your antiques out of my apartment.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Will both of you
please stop it?!

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: I'm... I'm sorry, Your Honor. I really am.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I knew she was gonna do that.
I felt it coming on.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: I mean, I felt... I knew it.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
You see, I don't wanna hurt
either one of them.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: They both, in their own ways...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...have made me
the happiest woman in the world.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - Come on, now, honey. Stop it.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Take your hands off her,

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Oh, yes, violence! Just the sort of behavior

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Why, you...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
So have I. Can't you see
that Nora is mine now?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: There's some in my refrigerator. I'll get it!

text:
Did I mention it was

text: All right, can we sit up, Mr. Fielding?

text:

text:

text: - Dan, are you okay to work?

...I have a little spinal irregularity

text: Charley, can we try to rearrange...?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
No trace.
Not a piece of fur, nothing.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Forget about the rabbit's foot.
It was an accident. It's gone.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Don't worry about it, I'm not.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
It's forgivable.

text:
Charley, I'm happy with you,

text: Tuna juice. Leaky bag in the garbage.

text:
I wanna see him and the Sedgewicks

text: I was hoping you'd say that.

text:
If you don't see what you want,

text: Bernie, It's not for me. It's for the DA.

text: And please, stop making a fuss over me.

text: Selma, I feel I have a lot to offer you.

text: That's why God gave us TV.

text: Selma, you're the kind of person...

text:
Bernie, I'm sure you're

text:

text:

text: So I lost my rabbit's foot.

text:
So what? It was more of a keepsake

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I won't. I won't. Careful.

So we've got a real toughie here,

text: - Not really, judge, the way I see it.

text:

text:

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
You're gonna feel silly

text:
I think your porch light's

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - I gotta go along with Mitch on that one.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
This may seem
a little untraditional at first...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...but trust me,
you'll get used to it.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...or working out
a sleeping schedule, but, hey...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...we're talking about
Nora's happiness, aren't we?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
That doesn't sound

text: - Charley, I want you to draft a document.

text:
Everybody ready?

text: - That won't be necessary, Your Honor.

text: I've decided to step out of the picture.

text:
I'm saying I just can't stand

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I'll never love anyone

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...but I'd rather give you up

text: - That's real decent of you, Dobie.

text:
You're just giving me up,

text: Takes a big man to do what he just did.

text:

text: I don't see anybody pressing them.

text:

text:
...and I know I can't

You're a pretty big guy

text:

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Well, I'm checking the classified of Soldier of Fortune magazine.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
But if I were you,

text:

text:
Don't worry.

text: No. I'll be all right. Really.

text:
But I can't promise that

text:
Well, 18 floors

text:
I figured if I stay off of it a week or so,

text:
